Heart failure typically isn't an acute problem. Heart failure happens when the heart can't inadequately pump/recieve blood. It literally means the heart fails as an effective pump. Right ventricular failure occurs when you have pulmonary hypertension. Thats when your body re routes blood from "useless" alveoli to more "useful" ones. This is seen typically in Chronic bronchitis sufferers, and are called "blue bloaters". Their right ventricle can no longer receive blood from circulation because of this rerouting of blood, causing a backup to systemic circulation. People live with this condition and walk around with it (not well I might add). There are also valvular problems that can attribute but I'm talking about the most common types.

Left ventricular failure is when hypertension causes the left ventricle to essentially become too jacked. Eventually the muscles will encroach on the interior of the ventricle (much like in right sided failure) and eventually the ejection fraction falls to a point where it's beats are no longer useful. Again, valvular problems can contribute to this but I'm talking about the more common types.
